#let para(body) = block(width: 100%)[#text(size: 20pt)[#body]]

#set text(font: "Arial", size: 9.2pt, fill: uga-black)
#set par(justify: true, leading: 0.53em)
#set list(indent: 8pt, body-indent: 5pt)

#grid(
  columns: (colw, colw, colw),
  column-gutter: gutter,
  align: top,

  [
    #sec[Background]
    #v(0.08in)
    #para[
      Quantifying ecosystem characteristics is the cornerstone of data-driven conservation and restoration policy, and multiple data streams are employed for this purpose. Biological sampling information, collected for example with trawl nets [1], has been used in concert with acoustic data, but there is recent interest in non-lethal, cost-effective [2] eDNA sampling as a tool to complement acoustic surveying. For instance, shifts in eDNA profiles accompanying organism movement as measured by acoustic sensors have been assessed [3], and paired hydroacoustic and eDNA surveys have been evaluated by replicating samples along the depth gradient of a pelagic lake habitat [4]. The current study investigates complementarity between eDNA, purse seine, and acoustic data gathered at three sites in July 2025 for quantification of ecosystem characteristics.
    ]


    #sec[Methods]
    #sub[Data collection]
    #para[
      #list(
        [Three sites (Oak Bay (Admiralty Inlet), Willow Island (San Juan Islands), and Squamish Harbor (Hood Canal)) were selected to capture a broad spatial extent within the Port Gamble Sklallam's usual and accustomed areas around the Salish Sea.],
        [At each site, purse seine captures were conducted by Long Live the Kings, The Tulalip Tribes, and United States Geological Survey using a commercial herring net. The approximate purse seine net dimensions were 402 meters long, fished effectively to 22 meters.],
        [Acoustic transects were performed using a 200 kHz, split-beam BioSonics scientific echosounder to capture an area approximately representative of the purse seine catch at each site.],
        [Concurrent eDNA samples were collected using a Niskin Rosette at six depths at a central point at each site.])
      ]
    #sub[Data analysis]
    #para[
    #list(
        [Acoustic survey data were processed in EchoView, and Sv integration results by 10-meter-squared cell were exported.],
        [Reads resulting from MiFish primer amplification were assigned using the Tronko algorithm [5], and taxonomic assignments with at most 10% divergence were retained.],
        [A combined data set was constructed with purse seine data indexed by site and with acoustic data and eDNA data indexed by site and 10-meter depth layer.],
        [Broader taxonomic categories were in some cases composed of data in more granular categories.]
    )
    ]
    #v(0.08in)
    #align(center)[#text(size: 20pt, weight: 700)[Map of the study area]]

    #v(0.07in)
    #sec[Conclusions]
    #para[
      #list(
        [Acoustic sampling may recapitulate seine results in terms of overall magnitude of biomass.],
        [eDNA surveys captured a broader suite of organisms than did seine surveys.],
        [eDNA results were useful in identifying species composition patterns within and between sites.],
        [eDNA sampling may have missed important species in sites that had greater depth extent than was sampled.],
        [eDNA read data is compositional and should be treated as a presence/absence metric; total reads do not 
        necessarily covary with acoustic backscatter.]
      )
      
    ]
